claims.claim: The closest structural contexts are verapamil and gallopamil, which share the 3,4-dimethoxyphenethyl-methylamino-propyl chain present in the query; verapamil fasted absolute oral bioavailability was 22% (17-29%) and gallopamil human bioavailability was 96.3%, both at or above the 20% threshold.
Verapamil in other conditions also gave F values above 20%: sustained-release fasted 49 ± 14%, sustained-release fed 34 ± 12%, and cirrhosis 30-52%.

Other structurally related basic drugs with similar physicochemical features, including drotaverine, bevantolol, and vernakalant, had mean absolute oral bioavailability values of 57-71%, all above 20%.
No L1 record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20%; the lowest mean value among the transferable contexts is verapamil fasted at 22%, which still meets the threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement for the exact query molecule is present in the supplied records.
No query-specific absorption, solubility, dissolution, first-pass, or formulation data are available.
Transfer from verapamil/gallopamil is structurally strong but not identical; the benzazepinone lactam modification could alter metabolism or permeability relative to the acyclic nitrile analogs.
The lowest relevant mean value (verapamil fasted, 22%) is close to the 20% threshold, so some quantitative uncertainty remains.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F >= 20%) because all transferable L1 records for closely related verapamil/gallopamil-type molecules report absolute oral bioavailability at or above 22%, and no affirmative evidence supports F < 20%; the mixed physicochemical prior is not sufficient to overturn this.
